question.text: In Young's double slit experiment the two slits are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> distance apart. Interference pattern is observed on a screen at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the slits. The first dark fringe is observed on the screen directly opposite to one of the slits. The wavelength of light will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
According to the question, the first dark fringe is observed directly opposite to one of the slits. Therefore, half of the fringe width is equal to half of the distance between the slits.

β2=d2⇒β=d=6 mm

⇒λDd=0.6×10-3⇒ λ=0.6×10-3dD⇒ λ=0.6×10-3×0.6×10-380×10-2

⇒λ=450×10-9 m=450 nm
